clinician.trajectory_summary: A 68-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B and HIV on highly active antiretroviral therapy (CD4 305 cells/µL, HIV viral load <20) presented with headache, generalized weakness, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and left eye ptosis with difficulty opening the eye. Physical examination confirmed left eye ptosis with the rest of the neurological examination unremarkable. Initial laboratory evaluation revealed mild transaminitis (AST 98, ALT 33), positive hepatitis B surface antigen and e-antigen, and hepatitis B viral DNA of 37,603. MRI of the abdomen identified a large 8.7×8.5 cm lesion in the right posterior hepatic lobe. CT of the head revealed sphenoid sinus opacification with a mass in the pituitary invading into the cavernous sinus, explaining the cranial nerve III involvement and ocular findings. Liver biopsy confirmed hepatocellular carcinoma. Transsphenoidal biopsy of the pituitary lesion revealed concordant findings of HCC, confirming metastatic disease. The patient received palliative whole-brain radiation (3000 cGy) over 10 days, which did not reverse the ophthalmoplegia. He was discharged to a subacute rehabilitation facility but died 2 weeks after discharge.
